The FOMC statement points to strong labor markets, robust household spending, and inflation near 2 percent with balanced risks and a steady path of gradual rate hikes. The Financial Stability Report tempers this by noting elevated valuations and rising corporate leverage. Incorporating SLOOS evidence further softens the outlook: banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans, tightened other terms across firm sizes, and reported weaker demand for construction and land development credit. This tilt toward tighter credit supply and softer loan demand suggests downside risk to business fixed investment already noted as moderating. Overall stance remains constructive but more cautious given emerging credit frictions.
